body.voice_description: A gravelly older male voice in his late sixties with a rough coastal British accent, weathered by salt and tobacco. Gruff, dry and snarky, slow to warm up, with a rasp and an occasional cough. Speaks in short barking sentences.
body.text: Eclipse, storm season, and the Saltgate howling. Of course they send a new money toff. Boiler's cold and the beacon's starving. Down to the engine room. Shovel coal, Isaac.

body.voice_description: A wiry, old male voice, reedy and thin, with a coastal sailor's accent. Wry and warm underneath, quick and frantic under pressure, voice cracking when he shouts over wind and an engine.
body.text: Easy now, we mean no harm. Just cold and wet. The gate, please? Good hands on that gate. Daniel, move. Quick, now.

body.voice_description: A young male voice in his early twenties, bright and enthusiastic, soft coastal accent. Light-hearted and chatty, with nervous laughs and a voice that thins and speeds up when anxious.
body.text: Down here suits me fine. Did the walls just... never mind. Warm is good. Arthur says it's just weather. I'm sure Arthur's right. He's usually right. Mostly.
